label: #3631337: Experimental error markers in forced colors (pinned parent MR)
description: Local AI-assisted proposal. Parent !17078 at c8136d010105a3c92fc4b20b9956eb31c703fc62 on both sides. Sequential comparison: #3631321 on both sides, then the experimental error-shape patch on After. Warnings and global error semantics remain open.
status: DRAFT: patch and CSS checks prepared; full Drupal and human review pending

steps.text: Standard install, Default Admin theme, form_test, and Article recipe on both sides. The pinned parent MR is present on both.
Open /admin/config/people/accounts at 1280px width. Enable forced colors, dark palette, and more contrast in the lab browser.
Select the first, a middle, and the last email tab. Inspect the first and last outer borders and both boundaries beside the selected tab in light and dark palettes.
steps.lookFor: Inactive tabs have dotted borders; the selected tab keeps solid borders.

steps.text: Open several email tabs and clear their required Subject fields, leaving a middle tab valid. Save, then select the valid middle tab. Inspect erroneous inactive tabs, then select an erroneous tab. Also submit the empty form_test details page and an Article with URL alias no-slash.
steps.lookFor: Double error bars across tabs, ordinary details, and sidebar accordion details. Icons and contains-error labels remain. This is a proposal for discussion, not a resolution of system-color semantics.

expected: Forced-color error bars are double across grouping elements, including selected erroneous tabs; selection remains independently identifiable.
actual: Error bars and selected-tab bars are both solid CanvasText; their principal border distinction is width.

checks.label: Vertical tabs exist at desktop width
Forced colors is active (enable it before running checks)
At least one tab contains a real validation error

observe.label: Selection is identifiable without relying on color
Keyboard focus remains visible and separate from validation errors
Icons, accessible error text, and narrow-screen details remain usable

manual: Real Windows contrast palettes, including a custom palette
LTR and real Farsi RTL; keyboard focus and error labels
First/middle/last selection, selected error, adjacent error, and hidden tabs
